*One merge-blocking finding* in `dedupe-imports` vs `main` (reviewed through `62644c3`):

*High — dedupe uses object identity instead of contact ID* — `src/dedupe.js:2`
`new Set(contacts)` only removes repeated references to the same object. Separate imports produce different objects with the same ID, so overlapping contacts survive in both `dedupe()` and `mergeImports()`, violating the README’s “one contact per id, keeping the first seen” contract.

Reproduced with:
```js
mergeImports(
  [{ id: 1, name: 'Ada' }],
  [{ id: 1, name: 'Ada updated' }]
)
// Actual: both contacts
// Expected: only the first contact
```

Track seen IDs and retain the first object for each ID. Add regression tests for distinct objects sharing an ID, both directly through `dedupe()` and across lists through `mergeImports()`.

*Validation:* All 4 existing tests pass, but the targeted overlap checks fail for both functions. The current dedupe test only repeats the same object reference, so it misses the core import scenario.

No files changed.
